detail.divText: Take it only if the role improves your trajectory, not merely your salary; relocation is too expensive for a shinier version of the same job. Does it give you better work, stronger people to learn from, or a clear path upward?

Don’t let the shiny title make the decision. Compare the actual work, growth, salary after relocation costs, and the life you’d have in that city—then notice whether the move feels expansive or merely impressive. If the pay were identical, which job would you choose?

Don’t decide on salary alone—compare the role, growth, cost of living, people you’d leave behind, and whether the new city gives you a life you actually want. My rule: if it moves you forward and the downsides are manageable rather than permanent, take the leap—chalo, scary can still be right. What’s the one thing making you hesitate most?
Dinnae judge the job title alone—compare the daily life it buys you against what the move would cost in money, support, and peace. If the pay were identical, would you still want to go?
Take it if the role moves you toward the life you want, not merely away from the one you’re bored with. Which matters more here: the work itself, the money, or the fresh start?

Don’t judge it by salary alone—compare the life around the job: growth, cost of living, people you’d leave, and whether the new city’s rhythm feels like somewhere you could breathe. If both options paid the same, which one would make you more curious to wake up six months from now?
